title: Discovered Check
subtitle: Double Checks, Seesaws, and the Unstoppable Masked Battery
summary: The tactical sibling of the pin: unleashing discovered checks, the devastating nature of double check, and the legendary windmill / seesaw combination.
aphorism: A discovered check is a pistol hidden behind a curtain. A double check is a thunderbolt that compels the king alone to flee.
attribution: 100th Anniversary Centenary Edition. Newly authored prose and interactive studies inspired by Aron Nimzowitsch (1925).

body.historicalContext: Nimzowitsch demonstrated that discovered checks are not random accidents, but the direct result of setting up masked batteries on open files and diagonals.

sections.title: The Masked Battery
sections.markdown:
A **discovered check** occurs when moving one piece unmasks a line of attack from a friendly bishop, rook, or queen standing behind it.

The moving piece is completely free to go anywhere — even to capture or deliver another [[threat]] — because the opponent is compelled to answer the [[check]] first!

engineLens.takeaway: Engines prioritize discovered-check batteries because they create multiple simultaneous tactical threats that overwhelm defensive resources.

sections.title: Double Check: The Unblockable Threat
sections.markdown:
When a discovered check is also a **double check** (both the unmasking piece and the battery piece give check simultaneously), it cannot be blocked and neither checking piece can be captured.

**The king must move.** Here White strikes with **1.Bxf7+ Ke7 2.Nxc6+!**, delivering a devastating discovered check from the queen on d1 while the knight wins Black's queen on d8.
